chunks: Ali ibn Ja'far narrated from his brother (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about a man who was performing Hajj al-Tamattu', who went out to Arafat and was unaware of entering the state of Ihram for Hajj on the Day of Tarwiyah, until he returned to his town. What is his status? He said: 'If he completes all the rituals, then his Hajj is complete.'

And I asked him about a man who forgot the Ihram for Hajj, then remembered it while he was at Arafat. What is his status? He said: 'He says: O God, according to Your Book and the Sunnah of Your Prophet, then his Ihram is complete.'

key_terms.الْإِحْرَامُ: Ihram (the state of consecration for pilgrimage)
key_terms.حَجُّ التَّمَتُّعِ: Hajj al-Tamattu' (a type of pilgrimage where one performs Umrah first, then Hajj)
key_terms.عَرَفَاتٍ: Arafat (the plain where the pillar of Hajj stands)
key_terms.يَوْمُ التَّرْوِيَةِ: The Day of Tarwiyah (8th of Dhu al-Hijjah)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a pilgrim who forgets to enter Ihram on the Day of Tarwiyah during Hajj al-Tamattu'?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), the juristic principle of *sahh al-hajj bi-l-fa'da* (validity of Hajj through completion despite initial defect) is applied to Hajj al-Tamattu'. The Imam distinguishes between a pilgrim who simply forgets the Ihram declaration and one who neglects it entirely, prescribing a specific verbal affirmation ('On Your Book and the Sunnah of Your Prophet') to rectify the state when remembered at Arafat, reflecting the Shia emphasis on intention and adherence to prophetic tradition in ritual purity.
